main_limitation: Not action-level and not high-stakes by itself; strongest for evidence-grounded text generation.
recommended_use: Use as the first hallucination/grounding dataset in the public uncertainty-control simulator.
source_note: RAGTruth focuses on hallucination in retrieval-augmented generation. It contains nearly 18,000 naturally generated RAG responses from multiple LLMs, manually annotated at both case and word level with hallucination intensity. It spans summarization, question answering, and data-to-text generation using news, open-domain web QA, and structured Yelp-style business data sources.

main_limitation: Reading-comprehension setting rather than agentic or high-stakes execution; strongest for abstention and missing-evidence behavior.
recommended_use: Use as the cleanest first dataset for demonstrating that a reliable AI system must know when not to answer.
source_note: SQuAD 2.0 combines answerable SQuAD questions with more than 50,000 adversarially written unanswerable questions. Systems must determine when no answer is supported by the paragraph and abstain.

main_limitation: Open-domain QA ambiguity rather than operational agent actions; requires careful mapping from ambiguity to clarification behavior.
recommended_use: Use to demonstrate that some AI reliability failures require clarification rather than better direct answering.
source_note: AmbigQA covers 14,042 NQ-open questions and requires finding every plausible answer plus rewriting the question to resolve ambiguity. The authors report that over half of NQ-open questions are ambiguous.

main_limitation: Focused on generated text factuality rather than action-level decision control.
recommended_use: Use for fine-grained factuality labels and claim-level mapping to supported, unsupported, or contradicted segments.
source_note: FELM annotates generated text segments, includes predefined error types, and provides reference links that support or contradict claims across world knowledge, math, and reasoning.

main_limitation: Long-form factual precision rather than agentic action control; source support can be expensive to verify.
recommended_use: Use to show why long outputs need claim-level control rather than single answer-level confidence.
source_note: FActScore decomposes generated long-form answers into atomic facts and measures what percentage are supported by reliable sources. The report reports that ChatGPT reached 58% factual precision on generated biographies in their human evaluation.

main_limitation: Uncertainty is inferred through sampling consistency; not a direct operational control dataset.
recommended_use: Use as supporting evidence that model inconsistency can be used as an uncertainty signal for hallucination detection.
source_note: SelfCheckGPT uses sampling consistency to detect hallucination: when a model knows a fact, sampled passages should be consistent; hallucinated facts tend to diverge or contradict each other. The authors manually annotated factuality of GPT-3-generated WikiBio passages.

main_limitation: Truthfulness/misconception benchmark rather than a direct uncertainty-control or agent-action dataset.
recommended_use: Use as supporting evidence that models can produce confident falsehoods, especially around common misconceptions.
source_note: TruthfulQA includes 817 questions across 38 categories such as health, law, finance, and politics. The original study found the best model truthful on 58% of questions while humans reached 94%.

main_limitation: Medical imaging is high-stakes and regulated; use as conceptual evidence for uncertainty management, not as a direct product claim unless proper domain validation exists.
recommended_use: Use to show that uncertainty labels exist in high-stakes real-world domains and that uncertain cases may require expert review.
source_note: CheXpert contains 224,316 chest radiographs from 65,240 patients, labels 14 observations from radiology reports, and captures uncertainty inherent in radiograph interpretation.

main_limitation: Distribution-shift benchmark rather than direct LLM/agent-control data; needs careful framing as robustness evidence.
recommended_use: Use to support the deployment-risk story: model reliability can degrade when deployment conditions differ from training/evaluation conditions.
source_note: WILDS contains 10 datasets reflecting real-world distribution shifts, including shifts across hospitals, camera traps, satellite imaging, poverty mapping, molecular data, civil comments, and other domains. Standard training yields substantially worse out-of-distribution than in-distribution performance.

main_limitation: Not specifically about LLM hallucination or agent actions; strongest for uncertainty estimation under realistic distribution shift.
recommended_use: Use to support the claim that uncertainty estimates and control decisions are needed under real distribution shifts.
source_note: Shifts is built to evaluate uncertainty estimates and robustness under real distributional shift across weather prediction, machine translation, and self-driving vehicle motion prediction.

main_limitation: General tool-agent trajectories rather than coding-agent authorization; useful for agent-step labeling patterns.
recommended_use: Use as the strongest public bridge from answer-level AI mistakes to process/action-level agent mistakes.
source_note: AgentProcessBench contains 1,000 diverse tool-using agent trajectories and 8,509 human-labeled step annotations, with reported 89.1% inter-annotator agreement.

main_limitation: Failure-trajectory oriented and not necessarily directly usable for general proceed/defer/block calibration without additional mapping.
recommended_use: Use for root-cause categories and failure taxonomy design in agentic systems.
source_note: AgentDebug introduces AgentErrorTaxonomy across memory, reflection, planning, action, and system-level operations, and constructs annotated failure trajectories from ALFWorld, GAIA, and WebShop.

main_limitation: Focused on failed trajectories and root-cause analysis; may not include enough successful/control examples for calibration without augmentation.
recommended_use: Use to design root-cause and escalation categories for agent workflows.
source_note: AgentRx manually annotates failed agent runs with a critical failure step and category across structured API workflows, incident management, and open-ended web/file tasks.

main_limitation: Tool-use error benchmark rather than full agentic workflow or coding-specific authorization.
recommended_use: Use for tool/action mistake categories such as wrong tool, wrong arguments, or premature tool use.
source_note: SpecTool characterizes seven LLM tool-use error patterns, addressing the gap that tool-use benchmarks often report only success rates without explaining failures.

dataset_name: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets
main_limitation: Meta-benchmark label-quality study rather than AI model-output control dataset.
recommended_use: Use to support caution around benchmark labels and to justify review/adjudication procedures in later evidence phases.
source_note: This study estimates at least 3.3% label errors on average across 10 common datasets and at least 6% in ImageNet validation, with human validation of algorithmically flagged errors.
